concepts.name: Projectile Motion: Range, Maximum Height & Flight Time
concepts.summary: 2D parabolic projectile motion under uniform downward gravity. Horizontal range $R = \frac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$, maximum height $H = \frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$, flight time $T = \frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$. Horizontal velocity $u\cos\theta$ remains invariant throughout.
concepts.common_traps: Horizontal range is identical for complementary angles $\theta$ and $(90^\circ - \theta)$, but maximum heights and flight times are different!
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Relation between Range and Max Height: $R = 4H\cot\theta$. At $\theta = 45^\circ$, $R = 4H$.

concepts.name: Relative Velocity in 2D (Rain-Man & River-Boat)
concepts.summary: Relative velocity $\vec{v}_{AB} = \vec{v}_A - \vec{v}_B$. Crossing a river in shortest time requires heading directly perpendicular to the bank ($t_{\min} = d/v_b$). Crossing along the shortest path (zero drift) requires swimming upstream at $\sin\theta = v_r/v_b$.
concepts.common_traps: To protect from vertically falling rain when walking forward, hold the umbrella tilted FORWARD in the direction of motion at $\tan\theta = v_m/v_r$.
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Shortest path across a river is only possible if swimmer speed $v_b > v_r$. If $v_b < v_r$, zero drift is impossible.

## 2. Comprehensive Concept Deep-Dive & Source PYQ Links

### 2.1 Projectile Motion: Range, Maximum Height & Flight Time (2D Kinematics)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **8 PYQs** (High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: 2D parabolic projectile motion under uniform downward gravity. Horizontal range $R = \frac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$, maximum height $H = \frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$, flight time $T = \frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$. Horizontal velocity $u\cos\theta$ remains invariant throughout.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
R = \frac{u^2 \\sin 2\\theta}{g}, \quad H = \frac{u^2 \\sin^2\\theta}{2g}, \quad R_{\max} = \frac{u^2}{g} \ (\text{at } \\theta=45^\\circ)
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Horizontal range is identical for complementary angles $\theta$ and $(90^\circ - \theta)$, but maximum heights and flight times are different!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Relation between Range and Max Height: $R = 4H\cot\theta$. At $\theta = 45^\circ$, $R = 4H$.

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2026 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"Two bodies are projected with the same velocity. If one is projected at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ and the other at $45^{\circ}$ to the horizo..."* — **Correct Answer: B**
- **[2025 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"In the projectile motion of a particle on a level ground, which of the following remains constant with reference to time and position?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2022 Shift] Q#3 (MCQ)**: *"Two objects are projected at an angle $\theta^{\circ}$ and $(90-\theta^{\circ})$ , to the horizontal with the same speed. The ratio of their..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2021 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"The trajectory of projectile is..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Relative Velocity in 2D (Rain-Man & River-Boat) (Relative Motion)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **1 PYQs** (Standard Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Relative velocity $\vec{v}_{AB} = \vec{v}_A - \vec{v}_B$. Crossing a river in shortest time requires heading directly perpendicular to the bank ($t_{\min} = d/v_b$). Crossing along the shortest path (zero drift) requires swimming upstream at $\sin\theta = v_r/v_b$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
t_{\min} = \frac{d}{v_b}, \quad \text{Shortest Path: } \\sin\\theta = \frac{v_{\text{river}}}{v_{\text{boat}}}, \quad \vec{v}_{\text{rain, man}} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_m
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: To protect from vertically falling rain when walking forward, hold the umbrella tilted FORWARD in the direction of motion at $\tan\theta = v_m/v_r$.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Shortest path across a river is only possible if swimmer speed $v_b > v_r$. If $v_b < v_r$, zero drift is impossible.

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2020 Shift] Q#4 (MCQ)**: *"Rain is falling vertically with a speed of $12ms^{-1}$ . A woman rides a bicycles with a speed of $12ms^{-1}$ in east to west direction. Wha..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Motion in a Plane

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
